 Fuel prices over $1 higher than last year with Election Day a week away
 By Aaron Barker FOX Local Money Published  October 27, 2026 11:50 AM CDT Share
 Copy Link 
 Email 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Reddit 
 Published  October 27, 2026 11:50 AM CDT Turnout Battle | Battleground Texas 
 The Texas Senate race heats up as new polling shows where James Talarico and Ken Paxton stand and which voters could decide the election.
 The Brief
 Prices of gasoline and diesel fuel remain higher than last year in Texas with Election Day one week away. 
 While higher than last year, prices for both have come down a bit since last month. 
 Voters say the economy is one of the top issues for them as they head to the polls. 
 DALLAS - With Election Day a week away, prices of both gasoline and diesel fuel remain higher than this time last year.
 By the numbers:
 According to AAA Texas, the average price for a gallon of regular gasoline Tuesday in the state is $3.71. That is 6 cents lower than last week and 21 cents lower than last month. However, that price is $1.11 per gallon higher than last year.
 For diesel prices, the margins from last year are even higher. AAA Texas reported the average price for a gallon of diesel fuel Tuesday is $5.75. That is 2 cents lower than last week and 13 cents lower than last month. Since last year, however, the price is $2.34 higher.
 A person pulls the gas pump out of their vehicle at a Shell gas station on August 03, 2023 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Brandon Bell/Getty Images) (Getty Images) 
 The lowest gas prices are concentrated in the Dallas-Fort Worth area and along the interstates 35 and 45 corridors. The highest gas prices are clustered in the Panhandle and West Texas
 Big picture view:
 Texas prices are much lower than the national average of $4.26 a gallon for gasoline and $6.35 per gallon for diesel.
 Economy still top issue for voters
 Dig deeper:
 Elevated fuel prices are just one part of the economic questions being mulled by Texas voters as Election Day approaches. 
 What they're saying:
 A recent poll by Emerson College found that most Texas voters are thinking about the economy when they cast their ballots.
 The results of the poll conducted between Oct. 17 and 19 found that 39% of Texas voters rank the economy as the top issue. That number was up 3 points from September, according to the poll.
 The poll found that the economy issue was followed by immigration (16%), threats to democracy (13%), education (12%) and healthcare (9%).
 Related
 article Economy remains top issue as Talarico, Paxton remain locked in tight race 
 James Talarico has a slight lead in the U.S. Senate race based on the latest Emerson College poll, but the race remains extremely close.
 When can I vote?
 What's next:
 Early voting in Texas ends Friday. Election Day is Nov. 3, and polls open in Texas at 7 a.m. 
 Related
 article Texas voting guide: Final week of early voting is underway. Here's what you should know 
 Early voting for the November election is underway. Voters can cast their ballots early through Friday, Oct. 30.
 The Source: Information in this story came from AAA Texas and Emerson College Polling.
